title: Hippocampus in Trauma
subtitle: Context, sequence and episodic memory
altText: Chalkboard-style clinical neuroscience diagram illustrating hippocampus in trauma across threat, memory, regulation and treatment systems.
learningObjectives: Explain hippocampus in trauma in clinically accurate language.
Distinguish established findings from theoretical or mixed claims in hippocampus in trauma.
Identify one limitation or safety implication relevant to hippocampus in trauma.

sections.explainSimply: The hippocampus helps place experiences in time and context.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Trauma may disrupt contextual discrimination, making safe present cues feel similar to past danger.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Hippocampal volume and function findings in PTSD are statistically reliable in some meta-analyses yet influenced by pre-existing risk, chronicity and comorbidity.
sections.thinkOfItLike: Think of hippocampus in trauma as one part of a dynamic safety-and-learning system rather than a single switch.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Psychologists need hippocampus in trauma to connect symptoms with learning, context, risk and treatment choice without reducing the person to a brain scan.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Smaller average volume does not prove trauma caused damage in one person.
sections.clinicalPearl: Clinical pearl: use hippocampus in trauma to sharpen formulation, not to replace phenomenology or outcome measurement.
sections.practicalExample: A clinician uses hippocampus in trauma to formulate triggers, state shifts, avoidance and functional impact, then monitors whether intervention improves daily life rather than relying on presumed neural change.
sections.limitationsCautions: Smaller average volume does not prove trauma caused damage in one person. Evidence classification: promising group evidence; causal uncertainty.
